Question ID: CW_U06_L05_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

A student is preparing a poem for digital publication. Which formatting choice best supports the genre?

answer.text: A. Put the entire poem in one paragraph so it uses less space.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A poem usually needs intentional line breaks and stanza breaks so the reader can follow image, sound, and pacing.

answer.text: B. Add random symbols before every line.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Decoration can distract readers if it does not support meaning.

answer.text: C. Remove the title because poems do not need one.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A title often prepares the reader for the poem's focus or tone.

answer.text: D. Keep the title clear and preserve purposeful line and stanza breaks.

feedback.text: Correct. This matches the poem's genre and helps the reader see how the poem moves.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L05_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

A short story draft appears as one long block of text with dialogue inside the same paragraph. What should the writer do first?

answer.text: A. Change every sentence to a different font.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Font changes do not solve the readability problem.

answer.text: B. Remove all dialogue marks.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This would make the dialogue harder to follow.

answer.text: C. Add paragraph breaks when the speaker changes and when the action shifts.

feedback.text: Correct. Paragraphing helps readers follow dialogue, action, and pacing in prose.

answer.text: D. Add extra blank lines after every sentence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random spacing can make the piece look unfinished.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L05_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

Which item best belongs in a final digital readiness check?

answer.text: A. Whether the file has a clear title, consistent spacing, and no leftover draft notes.

feedback.text: Correct. These checks help the piece look finished and readable.

answer.text: B. Whether the writer can explain every idea orally after submission.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The final digital version should be understandable without extra oral explanation.

answer.text: C. Whether the writer used the brightest possible color.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Color is not a substitute for clarity and format readiness.

answer.text: D. Whether the piece is longer than everyone else's.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length does not prove publication readiness. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L05_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

A script has character names written in several different styles. Which revision best improves publication formatting?

answer.text: A. Delete all character names.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Character names help the reader know who speaks.

answer.text: B. Use one consistent style for character labels and separate stage directions from dialogue.

feedback.text: Correct. Consistency helps readers or performers follow the scene.

answer.text: C. Add more stage directions without checking labels.

feedback.text: Incorrect. More content does not fix inconsistent formatting.

answer.text: D. Change the script into a poem.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The task is to format the script, not change genres.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L05_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

Which publication note best explains reader effect?

answer.text: A. I changed the format because it looked cool.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain how the format supports the reader.

answer.text: B. I used many decorations because publication means fancy.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Publication quality means reader-ready, not randomly decorated.

answer.text: C. I did not check spacing because the story is already finished.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Final formatting is part of preparing a finished piece.

answer.text: D. I revised paragraph breaks and dialogue spacing so the reader can follow the scene without rereading.

feedback.text: Correct. This names specific formatting choices and explains the reader effect.
